turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ag, give me a second, the screen's frozen. Mr Dlamini, I'm Doctor Naidoo. What's brought you in?
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, wrong tab. Upper or low?
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long's it been sore?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks. No. Since the move.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Few weeks. Can't remember the day.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Load shedding. It died. Down the stairs.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain there all the time?
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it go down the leg?
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any numbness or pins and needles?
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the mouse slipped. Numbness, yes or no?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Bakkie. Long drives. Goes dead.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any bladder trouble, wetting yourself, or you can't pass urine?
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the bowels, any loss of control?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Looser. Belt off at work. Not thinner.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cancer or TB in the family?
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): What painkillers are you on?
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nurse typed ibuprofen two hundred milligrams, three times a day. Is that it?
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): How often, then? Chart still says three times.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you getting both doses in, or missing some?
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else for the pain?
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): Capsules. Wife bought them at the chemist. Dunno the name.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Taking them at the moment?
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thinking out loud, don't mind the mumbling. Fridge lift, low backache, no solid red flags. Could be a muscle strain, could be a disc. I won't choose which today.
[SEG0064] person_1 (DOCTOR): Old note says one fifty over ninety. Ag, wrong line. Today's triage is one thirty two over eighty four, pulse seventy eight.
[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): Flexion's limited, the muscles beside the spine are tight, and the spine itself isn't tender. Straight leg raise is clear both sides.
[SEG0068] person_1 (DOCTOR): No x-ray today. If the leg goes weak, or the saddle area goes numb, or you can't pass urine, we scan the same day.
[SEG0070] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep moving, no bed rest. Take the Brufen with food. Don't use those green capsules until you bring me the box.
[SEG0072] person_1 (DOCTOR): You can add Panado, two tablets, one gram, up to four times a day if the ache breaks through.
[SEG0074] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll have reception book you for three weeks. Come sooner if it suddenly gets worse.
[SEG0076] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ag, shame about the parking this morning, the robots were out. This computer's going to die on me again, I can feel it.

spec.situation: Manual worker or office worker with low back pain for 'a few weeks or since the move'; doctor asks about red flags (numbness, bladder, weight loss, fever) one by one; patient answers some clearly, some vaguely or with a story. Painkiller use mentioned.
features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Patient reports looser pants and belt off; weight loss not absent.

omissions.text: Back pain is constant/present all the time.
Low back pain was triggered by carrying a fridge down the stairs during the move.
Numbness detail is recorded incompletely: the patient said the foot 'goes dead' sometimes during long drives in the bakkie.
Weight loss is recorded wrongly as absent: the patient reported looser pants/belt off at work, although he also said he was 'not thinner'.
Ibuprofen/Brufen dose was stated by the patient as 400 mg.
The doctor said no x-ray would be done today.

The doctor gave return precautions for new saddle numbness or inability to pass urine, and also said to come sooner if pain suddenly gets worse; after that the patient added 'Sharp,' suggesting sudden sharp worsening as a concern/clarification.
